editorial.description_en: The green of a stone that has been damp for a long time. Its hue sits on the warm-cool bisector, so the corpus records it as neutral rather than choosing a side.
editorial.description_ja: 長くしめった石のような、おだやかな緑。

provenance.derivation: Editorial construction, not a measurement. Specified in OKLCh as L 0.770, C 0.040, h 150.0° and converted to canonical D65 XYZ by @irodora/color-spaces 0.1.0 (oklchToXyz), rounded to six decimal places. Re-derivable from this sentence alone.
provenance.editorialNotes: Name coined by Irodora: 石 (ishi, stone) + 緑 (midori, green). It is not asserted to be a traditional Japanese colour name, and the hyphenated romaji marks it as a constructed compound (ADR-0065). "Stone Green" is an editorial decision about what communicates in English, not a literal translation of 石緑. Relations asserted from measured proximity under the current engine, not from a source: related is the three nearest in CIELAB — waka-shida at ΔE00 4.5, kawa-goke at ΔE00 5.5, tani-giri at ΔE00 7.5. complementary is empty because no entry in this corpus sits within 22° of the opposite hue. historicalVariants is empty: this entry makes no historical claim to vary from.
